Assessment incorporating economic-finance literature:
- Policy stance: The FOMC maintains the funds rate at 0–0.25% and continues sizable Treasury/MBS purchases, paired with outcome-based forward guidance under average-inflation targeting (AIT) that allows inflation to run moderately above 2% to anchor expectations at 2% over time.
- Transmission channels: New Keynesian frameworks (Clarida–Gali–Gertler; Woodford) emphasize that credible forward guidance and AIT work through expectations, lowering real rates and the output gap. Large-scale asset purchases operate via term-premium and signaling channels, affecting long-term yields and the slope of the curve (Cochrane–Piazzesi), while credit-channel effects (Bernanke–Gertler) support the flow of credit and market functioning noted in the statement.
- Credibility/time-inconsistency: Explicit AIT helps mitigate inflation bias (Barro–Gordon; Rogoff-style conservative central banker logic) and keep expectations anchored, aligning with the statement’s goal of well-anchored 2% expectations.
- Risks: The statement’s virus-related downside risks and sectoral weakness temper the tone. Literature (e.g., Orphanides on real-time mismeasurement) cautions that slack and inflation pressures can be misread, implying vigilance despite accommodation.

Net tone: Dovish and supportive of growth/markets via well-established channels, but moderated by acknowledged public-health risks. Overall slightly positive sentiment.
